gerrit-schotte.s: Gerrit Schotte is a Curaçao politician who became the first prime minister of Curaçao when it became an autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands on 10 October 2010. His government fell in 2012, and he was later convicted of corruption and money laundering.

gey-van-pittius.s: Nicolaas Claudius Gey van Pittius was a Boer administrator of the Land Goshen, a small republic proclaimed in 1882 at Rooigrond near Mafikeng by Boer freebooters who had fought for a Tswana faction. Goshen merged with Stellaland in 1883, but Britain's Warren Expedition ended…

ghalib-ibn-awad-al-quaiti.s: Ghalib ibn Awad al-Qu'aiti was the last sultan of the Qu'aiti Sultanate of Hadhramaut, succeeding his father in 1966. While he was abroad in September 1967, the National Liberation Front seized Mukalla, and the sultanate was abolished as South Yemen became independent.

ghayur-khan.s: Ghayur Khan was the ruler of Simsir, a Muslim principality in Chechnya, mentioned by Sharaf al-Din Yazdi and other chroniclers of Timur. He sided with Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde in his war with Timur, and Simsir was attacked by Timur's forces in 1395 during the campaign in…

ghazi-chelebi.s: Ghazi Chelebi was the last ruler of the Pervaneid principality of Sinop on the Black Sea coast of Anatolia, a descendant of the Seljuk minister Mu'in al-Din Pervane. He was famed for naval raids against the Genoese of Caffa and the Empire of Trebizond.

ghazi-muhammad.s: Ghazi Muhammad was an Avar scholar of the Naqshbandi order who became the first imam of Dagestan around 1828–1829. He preached holy war and strict sharia against Russian rule and local customary law, raiding Russian forts and towns such as Kizlyar.

ghazi-shah-chak.s: Ghazi Shah Chak was a Kashmiri noble who deposed the last Shah Mir sultan in 1561 and took the throne at Srinagar, founding the Chak dynasty, the first Shia dynasty of Kashmir. Illness forced him to hand power to his brother Husain Shah in 1563.

gheorghe-cantacuzino.s: Gheorghe Cantacuzino was a Wallachian boyar, son of Prince Șerban Cantacuzino, who served as the first ban of Craiova under Habsburg rule after Oltenia passed to Austria by the Treaty of Passarowitz in 1718. Imperial officials soon curtailed his authority as Vienna centralised…

gheorghe-gheorghiu-dej.s: Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej was the Communist leader of Romania from 1947 until his death in 1965. He nationalised industry, collectivised agriculture and imprisoned opponents in camps such as those on the Danube–Black Sea Canal.

gherardo-appiani.s: Gherardo Appiani was lord of Pisa who in 1399 sold the city to Gian Galeazzo Visconti of Milan while keeping Piombino, Elba and nearby islands for himself. This created the lordship, later principality, of Piombino, which his family ruled until the early 17th century.

ghiyath-al-din-muhammad.s: Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad was sultan of the Ghurid dynasty from 1163 to 1203, ruling from Firozkoh in the mountains of Ghor and later Herat. He shared power with his brother Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad, who led the conquests in northern India, while he himself fought the Khwarazmians…

ghiyath-al-din-pir-ali.s: Ghiyath al-Din Pir Ali was the last ruler of the Kart dynasty of Herat, reigning from 1370. He submitted to Timur, who took Herat in 1381 and deposed him.

ghulam-moinuddin-khanji.s: Ghulam Moinuddin Khanji was the last Khan of Manavadar, a small princely state in Kathiawar. In 1947 he acceded to Pakistan alongside the neighbouring Junagadh State.

gian-singh-rarewala.s: Gian Singh Rarewala was a Sikh politician and former official of Patiala State who served as chief minister of the Patiala and East Punjab States Union in 1951–1952 and again in 1954–1955. His Akali-supported coalition government of 1952 collapsed, leading to President's rule…

giberto-da-correggio.s: Giberto da Correggio was a noble of Parma who made himself lord of the city in 1303. A shifting ally of the Ghibellines and Guelphs, he extended his power over neighbouring cities for a time before being expelled from Parma in 1316.

gijsbert-karel-van-hogendorp.s: Gijsbert Karel van Hogendorp was a Dutch statesman who led the provisional government of November 1813 that ended French rule and invited William Frederick of Orange to return as sovereign prince. He drafted the constitution of 1814 and served as foreign minister, later…

gil-gavbara.s: Gil Gavbara was a prince from Gilan who, according to later tradition, took control of Tabaristan around 642 as the Sasanian Empire collapsed. He claimed Sasanian descent.

gil-gonzalez-davila.s: Gil González Dávila was a Spanish conquistador who led the first Spanish expedition into what is now Costa Rica and Nicaragua in 1522–1523. He met the chiefs of Nicoya and Nicarao, who accepted baptism, and gathered much gold.

gilbert-carter.s: Gilbert Carter was a British colonial administrator who served as governor of the Lagos Colony from 1891 to 1897. He forced a treaty on Ijebu after a military expedition in 1892 and toured the Yoruba interior in 1893, imposing peace terms that ended the long Yoruba wars…

gilbert-de-clare-1st-earl-of-pembroke.n: Gilbert de Clare, 1st Earl of Pembroke
gilbert-de-clare-1st-earl-of-pembroke.s: Gilbert de Clare, 1st Earl of Pembroke, was an Anglo-Norman baron created Earl of Pembroke by King Stephen in 1138, giving the lordship palatine powers. He supported Stephen during the Anarchy.

gilmar-pisas.s: Gilmar Pisas is a Curaçao politician who has been prime minister of Curaçao, a country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, since 2021. He leads the Movement for the Future of Curaçao party and previously headed an interim government in 2017.

giordano-pierleoni.s: Giordano Pierleoni was a member of the powerful Roman Pierleoni family and brother of the antipope Anacletus II. After the citizens of Rome rose against papal rule in 1143–1144 and revived the Senate on the Capitoline, he was named patrician, head of the new commune.

giorgio-iii-ghisi.s: Giorgio III Ghisi was the last Ghisi lord of Tinos and Mykonos in the Cyclades. When he died in 1390 he bequeathed the islands to the Republic of Venice, which ruled Tinos until it fell to the Ottomans in 1715.

giovanni-antonio-ranza.s: Giovanni Antonio Ranza was a Piedmontese priest-scholar turned Jacobin publicist who, with Ignazio Bonafous, proclaimed the short-lived Republic of Alba in April 1796 during Napoleon's first Italian campaign. The French did not support the venture, and it ended within days…

giovanni-di-vico.s: Giovanni di Vico was prefect of Rome and lord of Viterbo and much of northern Lazio in the mid-14th century, while the popes lived at Avignon. Cardinal Gil Álvarez de Albornoz defeated him in 1354 and restored papal authority over Viterbo, though he was allowed to keep some…

giovanni-ii-bentivoglio.s: Giovanni II Bentivoglio was the effective ruler of Bologna from 1463 to 1506, governing through the city's councils while keeping its formal ties to the Papal States. He was a patron of art and architecture.

giovanni-sforza.s: Giovanni Sforza was lord of Pesaro from 1483 and the first husband of Lucrezia Borgia, whom he married in 1493. Pope Alexander VI had the marriage annulled in 1497, and Cesare Borgia drove Giovanni from Pesaro in 1500.

girard-ii-of-roussillon.s: Girard II was the last count of Roussillon from the local dynasty, ruling from Perpignan. When he died without heirs in 1172, he left the county to Alfonso II of Aragon, count of Barcelona, bringing Roussillon into the Crown of Aragon.

girolamo-serra.s: Girolamo Serra was a Genoese patrician and historian who headed the provisional government of the restored Republic of Genoa in 1814. He lobbied the allies at the Congress of Vienna for its independence, but Genoa was annexed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1815.

gissur-thorvaldsson.s: Gissur Þorvaldsson was an Icelandic chieftain of the Haukdælir family and a leading figure of the Sturlung Age. He survived the burning of his farm at Flugumýri in 1253 and acted as an agent of King Haakon IV of Norway.

giulio-cesare-da-varano.s: Giulio Cesare da Varano was lord of Camerino from 1444, a condottiero and patron who rebuilt the ducal palace. In 1502 Cesare Borgia seized Camerino, and Giulio Cesare and several of his sons were strangled.

gjergj-thopia.s: Gjergj Thopia was lord of Durrës and the last ruler of the Thopia family's Principality of Albania, succeeding his father Karl Thopia in 1388. Under Ottoman pressure he handed Durrës to Venice in 1392, shortly before his death, and the rest of the Thopia lands later fell to…

gjon-kastrioti.s: Gjon Kastrioti was an Albanian lord who built a principality in the Mat valley and Dibër region, reaching towards the Adriatic near Lezhë. He accepted Ottoman overlordship while trading with Venice and Ragusa, and sent his sons as hostages to the Ottoman court.

gjon-zenebishi.s: Gjon Zenebishi was an Albanian chieftain who took the fortress of Gjirokastër around 1386 and ruled a principality in southern Albania and Epirus. He received the title of sebastokrator from the Despotate of Epirus and fought the Ottomans, who took Gjirokastër in 1418, the…

gleb-vasilkovich.s: Gleb Vasilkovich was the first prince of Beloozero, an appanage separated from Rostov in 1238 after his father Vasilko of Rostov was killed by the Mongols. He cooperated with the Golden Horde, married a Mongol princess and later also ruled Rostov.

gleb-vseslavich.s: Gleb Vseslavich was the first prince of Minsk, a son of Vseslav of Polotsk who received the town on his father's death in 1101. He fought the princes of Kiev and Vladimir Monomakh, who captured him in 1119.

glorious-revolution.s: The Glorious Revolution of 1688–1689 overthrew James II of England, whose Catholicism and absolutism had alienated his subjects. William of Orange landed with a Dutch army in November 1688, James fled, and Parliament offered the crown to William III and Mary II with the Bill…

glorious-revolution-spain.s: The Glorious Revolution of September 1868 was a military rising led by Generals Juan Prim and Francisco Serrano and Admiral Juan Bautista Topete that drove Queen Isabella II of Spain into exile. It opened the Sexenio Democrático, with universal male suffrage, the liberal…

gnaeus-cornelius-scipio-calvus.s: Gnaeus Cornelius Scipio Calvus was a Roman general who landed at Emporion in 218 BCE at the start of the Second Punic War, opening the Roman campaign in Hispania. He defeated Hanno and won over or subdued peoples north of the Ebro.

go-deokmu.s: Go Deokmu was a son of King Bojang, the last king of Goguryeo. In 699 the Tang court appointed him to govern the former Goguryeo population of the Liaodong region.

godfrey-i-of-louvain.s: Godfrey I of Louvain, called the Bearded, was Count of Louvain and Brussels and, from 1106, Duke of Lower Lorraine. Although he later lost the ducal office, his family kept the title and became the dukes of Brabant.

godred-crovan.s: Godred Crovan was a Norse-Gaelic warrior who, after surviving the Battle of Stamford Bridge in 1066, seized the Isle of Man in 1079 following a battle at Sky Hill. He founded the Crovan dynasty, which ruled Man and the Hebrides for nearly two centuries, and also held Dublin…

goias-velho.s: Goiás Velho, founded in 1727 as Vila Boa de Goiás during the gold rush of central Brazil, was the capital of the Captaincy of Goiás and later of the state of Goiás until 1937, when the capital moved to Goiânia. Its colonial churches and streets were declared a UNESCO World…

golden-bull-of-sicily.s: The Golden Bull of Sicily was a charter issued in Basel in 1212 by Frederick II, then King of Sicily and claimant to the German throne. It confirmed the hereditary royal title of Ottokar I of Bohemia and his successors and granted the Bohemian kings privileges within the Holy…

golden-gate-vladimir.s: The Golden Gate of Vladimir is the main surviving gate of the city walls of Vladimir, built in 1164 under Prince Andrei Bogolyubsky. Modelled on the Golden Gates of Kiev and Constantinople, it combined a defensive tower with a gate church.

golden-gate-bhaktapur.s: The Golden Gate of Bhaktapur is a gilded copper gateway at the entrance to the royal palace of fifty-five windows in Durbar Square, Bhaktapur, Nepal. Commissioned by King Ranajit Malla in 1754, it is decorated with images of the goddess Taleju and Garuda, and is one of the…

golden-horn.s: The Golden Horn is an inlet of the Bosporus in Istanbul that forms a deep natural harbour between the old city and Galata. It sheltered the shipping of Byzantium and Constantinople, and could be closed by a great chain in times of siege.

gomes-freire-de-andrade.s: Gomes Freire de Andrade, Count of Bobadela, was a Portuguese general who governed Rio de Janeiro from 1733 to 1763, at times also Minas Gerais and much of southern Brazil. He reorganised gold taxation and built public works such as the Carioca Aqueduct, and commanded the…

gongsun-du.s: Gongsun Du was appointed governor of Liaodong in 189 as the Han dynasty disintegrated, and made himself its independent ruler from Xiangping. He campaigned against Goguryeo and the Wuhuan and extended his control over the Han commanderies in northern Korea, founding the regime…

gongsun-kang.s: Gongsun Kang was the son and successor of Gongsun Du as ruler of Liaodong. Around 204 he created the Daifang Commandery south of Lelang in Korea, and in 207 he sent Cao Cao the heads of the fugitive Yuan brothers, Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi, securing recognition from the Han court.

gonka-ii.s: Gonka II was a ruler of the Velanati Chodas, a dynasty of chiefs in coastal Andhra. As Chola power in the Vengi region weakened in the 12th century, he ruled much of the land between the Krishna and Godavari rivers from Chandavolu, nominally under the Chola emperors but in…

gonzalo-pizarro.s: Gonzalo Pizarro was a Spanish conquistador and younger half-brother of Francisco Pizarro. He took part in the conquest of the Inca Empire and led an expedition to the Amazon in 1541.

gonzalo-portillo.s: Gonzalo Portillo was the last Spanish governor of Spanish Formosa, the colony in northern Taiwan centred on Keelung. With his garrison much reduced, he surrendered to a Dutch force in August 1642, and northern Taiwan passed to the Dutch East India Company's colony of Dutch…

gopal-singh-of-garrauli.s: Gopal Singh was a Bundela chief who resisted the British in Bundelkhand for several years after they took control of the region in 1803. In 1812 he submitted and received Garrauli and nearby villages by sanad as a hereditary holding, founding the small princely state of Garrauli.

gopalrao-patwardhan.s: Gopalrao Patwardhan was a member of the Patwardhan family of Maratha military commanders who became the first ruler of Jamkhandi State when the family's lands in the Southern Maratha Country were divided in 1811. Jamkhandi remained a princely state under the British until it…

gottfried-heinrich-graf-zu-pappenheim.s: Gottfried Heinrich Graf zu Pappenheim was a Bavarian-born field marshal of the Catholic League and the Holy Roman Emperor during the Thirty Years' War. A convert to Catholicism, he became famous as a bold cavalry commander, took part in the sack of Magdeburg in 1631 and was…

govardhan-chand.s: Govardhan Chand was Raja of Guler, a small Rajput hill state in the Kangra region of the western Himalayas, in the mid-18th century. His court patronised the painter Pandit Seu and his sons Manaku and Nainsukh, whose refined, naturalistic work founded the Guler style of Pahari…

govinda-iii.s: Govinda III was a king of the Rashtrakuta dynasty of the Deccan, the son of Dhruva. He led campaigns as far north as the Ganges plain and the Himalayan foothills, defeating the Gurjara-Pratihara king Nagabhata II and receiving the submission of the Pala ruler Dharmapala.

govindachandra-of-the-chandra-dynasty.s: Govindachandra was the last notable king of the Chandra dynasty of eastern Bengal in the early 11th century. Inscriptions of the Chola king Rajendra I record that his northern expedition of around 1021–1024 defeated Govindachandra of Vangala on its march to the Ganges.

govindachandra-of-the-gahadavala-dynasty.s: Govindachandra was the most powerful king of the Gahadavala dynasty, which ruled from Kannauj and Varanasi in northern India. He fought the Palas of Bengal and resisted Ghaznavid raids, and he issued more land grants than any other ruler of his line.

goz-beida.s: Goz Beida is a town in the Ouaddaï highlands of south-eastern Chad, near the border with Sudan. It became the seat of the sultans of Dar Sila, a small Muslim sultanate that paid tribute to its larger neighbour Wadai.

gran-sasso.s: The Gran Sasso d'Italia is the highest massif of the Apennines, in Abruzzo, central Italy, rising to 2,912 metres at Corno Grande. In antiquity its valleys were home to the Vestini.

grand-bahama.s: Grand Bahama is the northernmost of the larger islands of the Bahamas, lying about 90 kilometres off the coast of Florida. Its main town, Freeport, was developed from 1955 as a free-trade zone and became the country's second city and a centre of tourism, shipping and industry.

grand-duke-konstantin-pavlovich-of-russi.n: Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich of Russia
grand-duke-konstantin-pavlovich-of-russi.s: Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich was the second son of Emperor Paul I of Russia and brother of Alexander I and Nicholas I. From 1815 he was commander-in-chief of the army of Congress Poland and its effective governor, ruling harshly and ignoring the kingdom's constitution.

grand-port.s: Grand Port is a large bay and harbour on the south-east coast of Mauritius, on which the town of Mahébourg now stands. The Dutch East India Company built its first settlement, Fort Frederik Hendrik, there in 1638.

geza-grand-prince-of-the-hungarians.n: Géza, Grand Prince of the Hungarians
geza-grand-prince-of-the-hungarians.s: Géza was Grand Prince of the Hungarians from about 972 until his death in 997, a member of the Árpád dynasty. He made peace with the Holy Roman Empire, invited Western missionaries and was baptised, beginning the conversion of the Hungarians to Latin Christianity.

grand-village-of-the-natchez.s: The Grand Village of the Natchez is an archaeological site on St Catherine Creek in Natchez, Mississippi, the main ceremonial centre of the Natchez people in the late 17th and early 18th centuries. It holds platform mounds on which stood the house of the Great Sun, the sacred…

grand-village-of-the-illinois.s: The Grand Village of the Illinois was a large settlement of the Kaskaskia and other Illinois peoples on the upper Illinois River, opposite Starved Rock in present-day Illinois. Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet visited it in 1673, and it then held thousands of people in many…

granville-sharp.s: Granville Sharp was an English scholar and campaigner, one of the first British activists for the abolition of the slave trade. He brought legal cases on behalf of enslaved Africans, including that of James Somerset in 1772.

great-courland-bay.s: Great Courland Bay is a bay on the north-west coast of Tobago in the Caribbean, near the village of Plymouth. Settlers sent by Duke Jacob Kettler of Courland landed there in 1654 and built Fort Jacobus, founding the colony of New Courland.

great-depression.s: The Great Depression was the worldwide economic slump that followed the Wall Street Crash of October 1929 and lasted through much of the 1930s. World trade and commodity prices collapsed, causing mass unemployment and bank failures.

great-illyrian-revolt.s: The Great Illyrian Revolt was a rising of the peoples of Pannonia and Dalmatia against Roman rule from 6 to 9 CE. It began when Rome levied troops for a war against the Marcomanni and was led by two men named Bato, of the Daesitiates and of the Breuci.

great-syrian-revolt.s: The Great Syrian Revolt was a rising against French Mandate rule in Syria and Lebanon from 1925 to 1927. It began in the Jabal al-Druze under Sultan al-Atrash and spread to Damascus and other regions, where nationalists joined it.

great-turkish-war.s: The Great Turkish War was fought between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy League of the Habsburgs, Poland-Lithuania, Venice and Russia from 1683 to 1699. It began with the failed Ottoman siege of Vienna and saw the Habsburgs conquer Hungary, Slavonia and Transylvania while…

great-zab.s: The Great Zab is a river rising in the mountains of south-eastern Turkey and flowing through Iraqi Kurdistan to join the Tigris south of Mosul. Its valleys formed the heartland of Kurdish principalities such as Bahdinan and Soran.

greater-hamburg-act.s: The Greater Hamburg Act was a Nazi German law of 1937 that redrew the boundaries of several northern German states. It enlarged Hamburg with Altona, Wandsbek and Harburg-Wilhelmsburg, ended the independence of the Free City of Lübeck, and transferred Oldenburg's exclaves of…

greater-kabylia.s: Greater Kabylia is the mountainous Berber region of northern Algeria centred on the Djurdjura range, east of Algiers, with Tizi Ouzou as its main town today. Its Kabyle villages long kept strong self-government.

gregoire-kayibanda.s: Grégoire Kayibanda was the first President of Rwanda, from 1962 to 1973. A Hutu journalist and leader of the Parmehutu party, he co-wrote the Hutu Manifesto of 1957 and led the revolution that overthrew the Tutsi monarchy.

gregory-the-patrician.s: Gregory the Patrician was the Byzantine exarch of Africa and a relative of the Heraclian dynasty. Opposing the Monothelete religious policy of Constans II, he proclaimed himself emperor in 646.

grigol-dadiani.s: Grigol Dadiani was Prince of Mingrelia in western Georgia, ruling with interruptions from 1788 to 1804. Contested by rival relatives and pressed by the King of Imereti, he placed his principality under the protection of the Russian Empire in 1803.

grimoald-alferanites.s: Grimoald Alferanites was a citizen of Bari who seized power in the city in 1119, during the weak rule of the Norman duke William II of Apulia, and styled himself prince. He governed Bari as an independent lordship for over a decade.

gruffydd-maelor-i.s: Gruffydd Maelor I was a Welsh prince who ruled northern Powys after the death of his father, Madog ap Maredudd, the last king of all Powys, in 1160. His territory, centred on Maelor and Ial, became the principality later named Powys Fadog after his son Madog ap Gruffydd Maelor.

guadalupe-victoria.s: Guadalupe Victoria, born José Miguel Fernández y Félix, was a general of the Mexican War of Independence and the first President of Mexico, from 1824 to 1829. He took his adopted name in honour of the Virgin of Guadalupe and of victory.

guan-yu.s: Guan Yu was a general of the late Han dynasty and a sworn companion of Liu Bei, founder of Shu Han. He held Jing province for Liu Bei until Sun Quan's forces under Lü Meng seized it in 219; he was captured and executed early in 220.

guanabara-bay.s: Guanabara Bay is a large bay on the south-eastern coast of Brazil, on whose shores stand the cities of Rio de Janeiro and Niterói. In 1555 French settlers under Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon founded France Antarctique on an island in the bay.

guglielmo-embriaco.s: Guglielmo Embriaco was a Genoese merchant and commander in the First Crusade. In 1099 he dismantled his ships to build siege engines for the capture of Jerusalem, and he later helped take Arsuf and Caesarea, bringing rich booty back to Genoa.

guhyeong-of-geumgwan-gaya.s: Guhyeong was the last king of Geumgwan Gaya, the leading state of the early Gaya confederacy in southern Korea, centred on modern Gimhae. In 532 he surrendered his kingdom to Silla and was received into the Silla aristocracy with his family.

guido-novello-da-polenta.s: Guido Novello da Polenta was lord of Ravenna from 1316 to 1322 and a poet and patron of letters. He welcomed the exiled Dante Alighieri to his court, where Dante completed the Divine Comedy before dying in Ravenna in 1321.

guido-pallavicini.s: Guido Pallavicini was an Italian knight from the Pallavicini family of Lombardy who joined the Fourth Crusade. In 1204 Boniface of Montferrat, King of Thessalonica, granted him Bodonitsa above the pass of Thermopylae, and he became its first marquis.

guido-tarlati.s: Guido Tarlati was Bishop of Arezzo from 1312 and lord of the city from 1321 until his death in 1327, leading the Ghibelline party in Tuscany. He expanded Arezzo's territory, rebuilt its walls and crowned Louis the Bavarian King of Italy in Milan in 1327, despite papal…

guido-torelli.s: Guido Torelli was an Italian condottiere who served the Visconti dukes of Milan and commanded their forces in several wars. In 1406 he received the town of Guastalla on the Po, later raised to a county, and he also held Montechiarugolo.

guigues-i-of-albon.s: Guigues I, known as Guigues the Old, was a count of Albon in the Kingdom of Arles who from about 1029 gathered lands in the Viennois, the Grésivaudan and around Grenoble. He founded the house of Albon, whose counts took the name Dauphin in the 12th century, giving the region…

guillaume-farel.s: Guillaume Farel was a French evangelist and Protestant reformer who spread the Reformation in French-speaking Switzerland. He preached at Montbéliard in 1524–1525, brought Neuchâtel to Protestantism in 1530 and helped win Geneva in 1535, where he persuaded John Calvin to stay…

guillem-ii-of-pallars-sobira.s: Guillem II was the first count of Pallars Sobirà, a mountain county in the Catalan Pyrenees. When his father Sunyer of Pallars divided his lands in 1011, Guillem received the upper valleys of the Noguera Pallaresa around Sort and Àneu, while his brother Ramon III took Pallars…

guled-abdi.s: Guled Abdi was the first sultan of the Isaaq Sultanate in northern Somaliland, chosen by the Isaaq clans in the mid-18th century after their victory at the battle of Lafaruug. He belonged to the Eidagale clan, and his descendants, the Rer Guled, kept the title with their seat…

gulf-of-bone.s: The Gulf of Bone is a large gulf of the Flores Sea between the south-western and south-eastern peninsulas of Sulawesi, Indonesia. Its coasts were the heartland of Bugis kingdoms: Luwu at its head was considered the oldest, and Bone, based at Watampone on the western shore,…

gulf-of-khambhat.s: The Gulf of Khambhat is an inlet of the Arabian Sea in Gujarat, western India, separating the Kathiawar peninsula from the mainland. It has some of the highest tides in the world.

gulf-of-mannar.s: The Gulf of Mannar is a shallow bay of the Indian Ocean between south-eastern India and north-western Sri Lanka, bounded by Adam's Bridge to the north. Its pearl oyster beds were fished from ancient times and enriched the Pandya kingdom, whose port of Korkai traded with Rome.

gulf-of-salerno.s: The Gulf of Salerno is an inlet of the Tyrrhenian Sea in Campania, southern Italy, between the Sorrento peninsula and the Cilento coast. Its shores held the Greek city of Poseidonia (Paestum) and later Salerno.

gulf-of-sirte.s: The Gulf of Sirte is a large gulf of the Mediterranean on the coast of Libya, between Tripolitania and Cyrenaica, known in antiquity as the Greater Syrtis. Its shallow waters and shifting sands were feared by ancient sailors, and its desert shore long divided the Punic and…

gulf-of-taranto.s: The Gulf of Taranto is a gulf of the Ionian Sea in southern Italy, between the heel and toe of the peninsula. In the 8th and 7th centuries BCE Greek colonists founded cities on its shores, including Taras (Taranto), Metapontum, Sybaris and Croton, which formed part of Magna…

gulf-war.s: The Gulf War was the conflict that followed Iraq's invasion and annexation of Kuwait in August 1990. A coalition of 35 states led by the United States assembled forces in Saudi Arabia and, after an air campaign from January 1991, drove the Iraqi army out of Kuwait in a short…

guman-singh.s: Guman Singh was a Bundela chief descended from Chhatrasal, the founder of Panna. Around 1765 he received a share of the family lands in Bundelkhand, with his seat at Banda.

gunther-victor-prince-of-schwarzburg.s: Günther Victor was Prince of Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt from 1890 and, after the death of his cousin in 1909, also of Schwarzburg-Sondershausen, ruling the two states in personal union. He abdicated in November 1918 for Rudolstadt and Sondershausen, among the last German monarchs…

gunzelin-of-hagen.s: Gunzelin of Hagen was a Saxon nobleman and vassal of Henry the Lion, Duke of Saxony. After Henry conquered the Obotrite lands, he made Gunzelin governor of Schwerin and in 1167 created the County of Schwerin for him.

gurbakhsh-singh-of-kalsia.s: Gurbakhsh Singh was a Sikh sardar of the Sandhu Jat clan from the village of Kalsia near Lahore and a member of the Karorsinghia misl. Around 1760 he seized territory south of the Sutlej around Chhachhrauli.

gurbanguly-berdimuhamedow.s: Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow is a Turkmen politician, a dentist by training, who became President of Turkmenistan after the death of Saparmurat Niyazov in 2006. He ruled as an authoritarian leader and built a personality cult of his own, with the title Arkadag (Protector).

gurdit-singh-of-ladwa.s: Gurdit Singh was a Sikh sardar who seized Ladwa and nearby lands near Kurukshetra around 1763, when the Sikh misls overran the Mughal province of Sirhind. His chiefship became one of the Cis-Sutlej states under British protection from 1809.

gurgen-king-of-the-iberians.s: Gurgen was a Georgian Bagratid prince of Tao-Klarjeti who held the title King of Kings of the Iberians from 994 until his death in 1008. He was the father of Bagrat III, who was adopted by David III Kouropalates and inherited Abkhazia through his mother.

gurgen-i-of-lori.s: Gurgen, also known as Kiurike I, was the son of King Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia and founder of the Kingdom of Lori, also called Tashir-Dzoraget, in northern Armenia. Around 979 he received the northern provinces and took the title of king, founding the Kiurikian dynasty.

gustav-adolph-duke-of-mecklenburg-gustro.s: Gustav Adolph was the last Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow, reigning from 1636 under a regency and in person from 1654 until his death in 1695. A Lutheran ruler, he rebuilt a land devastated by the Thirty Years' War.

gustav-iv-adolf.s: Gustav IV Adolf was King of Sweden from 1792 to 1809. A determined enemy of Napoleon, he joined the coalitions against France, abolished serfdom in Swedish Pomerania in 1806 and lost the territory to French occupation in 1807.

gustav-nachtigal.s: Gustav Nachtigal was a German physician and explorer who travelled through the Sahara and the central Sudan between 1869 and 1874, visiting Bornu, Wadai and Bagirmi. In 1884, as imperial commissioner for West Africa, he signed protection treaties that established German rule…

gusti-ketut-jelantik.s: Gusti Ketut Jelantik was the patih (chief minister) of the Balinese kingdom of Buleleng and the leader of its resistance to the Dutch. He refused Dutch demands over the plundering of shipwrecks and in 1848 defeated a Dutch expedition at the fortress of Jagaraga.

gusti-ngurah-agung.s: Gusti Ngurah Agung was the last raja of the Balinese kingdom of Tabanan. In 1906, after the Dutch conquest of Badung and its puputan, Dutch troops advanced on Tabanan and he surrendered.

gusti-panji-sakti.s: Gusti Panji Sakti was a Balinese warrior noble of the Gelgel court who founded the kingdom of Buleleng on the north coast of Bali around 1660. He made Singaraja his capital and extended his power across the Bali Strait to Blambangan in eastern Java.

gwanggaeto-the-great.s: Gwanggaeto the Great was the nineteenth king of Goguryeo, reigning from 391 to 413. He conquered wide lands in Manchuria from the Later Yan and the Khitan, defeated Baekje, and sent an army to help Silla against Wa (Japanese) and Gaya forces in 400.

gyula-andrassy.s: Count Gyula Andrássy was a Hungarian statesman who, after fighting in the revolution of 1848–1849 and years in exile, negotiated the Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867 with Ferenc Deák. He became the first Prime Minister of Hungary under the Dual Monarchy, from 1867 to 1871,…

gyula-the-younger.s: Gyula the Younger was the last independent gyula, or ruler, of Transylvania, the maternal uncle of Stephen I of Hungary. He kept a separate realm oriented towards Byzantium and resisted Stephen's authority.

green-corn-ceremony.s: The Green Corn Ceremony is the most important annual festival of the Muscogee (Creek), Seminole and other peoples of the south-eastern woodlands of North America. Held in midsummer when the new maize ripens, it is a rite of renewal: fires are extinguished and relit, offences…

geunchogo-of-baekje.s: Geunchogo was king of Baekje from 346 to 375, the period of its greatest early power. He subdued the remaining Mahan statelets of south-western Korea, extended Baekje's influence towards the Gaya region and in 371 attacked Goguryeo, killing its King Gogugwon at Pyongyang.

gojong-of-korea.s: Gojong was the 26th king of the Joseon dynasty from 1863 and the first emperor of the Korean Empire, which he proclaimed in 1897. His reign saw the forced opening of Korea by the Treaty of Ganghwa, the murder of Queen Min and growing Japanese domination.

gyanendra-of-nepal.s: Gyanendra was the last King of Nepal, reigning from 2001 to 2008. He came to the throne after the royal massacre of June 2001 killed his brother King Birendra and much of the royal family.

gerard-lake-1st-viscount-lake.s: Gerard Lake, 1st Viscount Lake, was a British general who became commander-in-chief in India in 1801. In the Second Anglo-Maratha War he defeated the Marathas at Delhi and Laswari in 1803, bringing Delhi and the Mughal emperor under British protection.

george-carteret.s: Sir George Carteret was a Jersey-born royalist naval officer who held Jersey for Charles I and became a courtier after the Restoration. In 1664 he and John Berkeley received the land between the Hudson and Delaware rivers, named New Jersey after his island; after its division…

gilbert-elliot-1st-earl-of-minto.s: Gilbert Elliot, 1st Earl of Minto, was a Scottish politician and diplomat. He served as viceroy of the Anglo-Corsican Kingdom from 1794 to 1796, governing from Bastia under a British-backed constitution, until the British evacuated the island.

gaius-suetonius-paulinus.s: Gaius Suetonius Paulinus was a Roman general and governor of Britain from about 58 to 61 CE. He campaigned in Wales against tribes such as the Ordovices and attacked the druid centre on Anglesey in 60 CE.
